These are seismological chapters: intensity tables, felt reports, hypocenter tables and a layered P-wave velocity model (table 2, p. 76) have no fields in the extraction schema and were not recorded. Recorded only structural interpretations (seismic zones, the November 22, 1974 nodal plane, Taber's hypothesized buried fault) and South Carolina references. Chapter D continues into packet-03 (its reference list starts on p. 80). Skipped general seismology references (attenuation, magnitude, California, Europe, eastern Tennessee).
Pages 81-115: end of chapter D references, all of chapter E (Gohn and others, lithostratigraphy of CCC 1, pp. 87-98, the cataloged chapter) and the first part of chapter F (Hazel and others, biostratigraphy, pp. 103-115; continues in packet-04). Each formation has two unit entries: one from chapter E (lithology, thickness, contacts) and one from chapter F (ages, fossils, paleoenvironment). The chapter F summary table (p. 103) gives 6 m for the Pleistocene(?) unit where chapter E gives 5 m (16 ft); only the chapter E value was recorded. Chapter A (packet-01) says CCC 1 was drilled in 1974 and 1975; chapter E says January-March 1975; both recorded on their pages. References: recorded chapter E's South Carolina references (p. 98); skipped North Carolina, New Jersey, Alabama references and the duplicate Colquhoun and Johnson (1968) already recorded from chapter A.

Long species lists and palynological/dinoflagellate zone correlations with New Jersey and Maryland units were not transcribed. Major-oxide, trace-element and K-Ar tables (tables 1-4) have no schema fields and were not recorded except the K-Ar age interpretation. Several chapter G pages have interleaved columns, so quotes were kept short. References: chapter F list recorded only Sanders (1974), the one South Carolina reference not already recorded from other chapters (Cooke 1936, Pooser 1965 and Swift and Heron 1969 are duplicates); chapter G references follow in packet-05.
Pages 142-177: end of chapter G (geochemistry of CCC 1 basalt, references), chapter H (Sass and Ziagos, heat flow in CCC 1) and first part of chapter I (Popenoe and Zietz, geophysical basement; continues in packet-06). Recorded: South Carolina wells that reached basement from chapter I table 1 (pp. 165-166; Georgia and North Carolina wells skipped), each with basement rock type and basement altitude (meters, negative = below sea level; stored as interval description because it is an altitude, not a depth); basement belts and plutons; geophysically interpreted faults, dikes, arches and basins; the Middendorf heat-flow/ground-water observation. Not recorded: geochemical discrimination diagrams, heat-flow table values, gravity/magnetic anomaly descriptions without named features. Well 12's location is printed '8 km SW of Aiken County, S.C.'. References: only South Carolina items not already recorded (Zietz and others 1976; Ziagos and others 1976); chapter G's reference list is otherwise general geochemistry.
Pages 178-217: end of chapter I (Popenoe and Zietz), chapter J (Phillips, magnetic basement) and chapter K (Long and Champion, Bouguer gravity of the Summerville-Charleston epicentral zone). Content is geophysical interpretation; recorded interpreted structures (dikes, plutons, faults, basins), basement depths and the deep Summerville well. Pages 178-179 have two columns interleaved in the text layer, so quotes there are short fragments. Model parameters (cylinder/sphere radii, density contrasts, gravity gradients) were not recorded. References: South Carolina items from chapter I's list (pp. 180-181) not already recorded from other chapters; chapters J and K references (aeromagnetic map 75-590 already recorded; K continues in packet-07) skipped here.
Pages 218-272: end of chapter K references, chapter L (Ackermann, seismic refraction), chapter M (Talwani, quarry-blast crustal model), chapter N (Campbell, resistivity soundings) and chapter O (Kane, gravity highs and earthquake centers). Mostly geophysical; recorded interpreted structures, unit seismic/electrical properties, a freshwater-saltwater interface estimate and South Carolina references. Not recorded: VES layer table (p. 260), traveltime curve parameters, gravity model densities, chapter O comparisons with other eastern US earthquake areas. Two quotes about the quarries' Santee Limestone lithology (p. 237) could not be matched to the interleaved text layer and were dropped. Chapter N footnote on the second corehole (basalt 774-1,031 m, 257 m thick) duplicates CCC 3 data recorded in packet-01.
